MerchantProductUrlLookupResponse.description:
Source-aware product URL lookup result.

Indexed results retain catalog ownership and a complete indexed product view.
On-demand and client-HTML results use the same product DTO without
fabricating indexed identity or lifecycle state: ``client_html`` results
come from ``POST /products/resolve-from-html``, where the caller supplied
the page bytes and nothing was fetched or cached.

canonicalUrl.description: For catalog_extractor results this is null unless page-declared evidence is available. For shallow on-demand and client_html results: the canonical URL the product page declares (JSON-LD Product/variant url, link rel=canonical, selected Offer.url, or og:url); when the page declares none the resolver falls back to the final fetched URL (on-demand) or the caller-supplied url (client_html), so a non-null value is not proof of a declaration. Null for indexed results — we do not yet store the page-declared canonical for indexed products. For follow-up lookups use normalizedUrl (indexed, catalog_extractor, and client_html results) or resolvedUrl (shallow on-demand results), not this field.
canonicalUrl.title: Canonicalurl

matchedVia.description: Debug: which probe arm of the URL lookup ladder resolved the product — normalized_alias | exact | normalized_exact | loose | structural_alias | learned_alias:<rule_id>. Absent for on-demand results and legacy paths. Informational only; values may be extended.
matchedVia.title: Matchedvia

normalizedUrl.description: Stable URL for this product that callers should reuse on follow-up lookups. For indexed results this is the matched product's stored normalized URL, falling back to its exact indexed URL for legacy rows. For client_html results it is Octogen's deterministic normalization of requestedUrl, falling back to canonicalUrl when the caller supplied no URL. That normalization forces https, strips leading www., fragments and known tracking params, and sorts remaining query params. For catalog extraction it uses shared normalization; for shallow on-demand results reuse resolvedUrl instead.
normalizedUrl.title: Normalizedurl

requestedUrl.description: The URL the caller submitted, echoed verbatim. For client_html results this is the variant-qualified identity: storefronts commonly record a shopper's variant selection only in URL query parameters, and canonicalUrl conventionally drops them — key on this field when variants must stay distinct.
requestedUrl.title: Requestedurl

resolvedUrl.description: Final fetched URL for shallow resolution; crawler-accepted URL for catalog extraction. Populated for on-demand results only.
resolvedUrl.title: Resolvedurl

warnings.description:
Stable, deduplicated warning codes for on-demand and
client-HTML results. Renames or removals are breaking changes; clients should
tolerate unknown additions. Current successful-response vocabulary:

| Code | Overview |
| --- | --- |
| `source_url_missing` | The client-HTML request omitted `url`. |
| `multiple_product_nodes` | Multiple JSON-LD product candidates were found; the strongest was selected. |
| `variant_url_no_match` | The selected candidate URL did not match the submitted URL; this can be a sibling product or the same product with query parameters dropped. |
| `malformed_json_ld` | At least one malformed JSON-LD block was skipped. |
| `canonical_invalid` | The page declared a canonical URL with an unusable hostname—often because two URLs were accidentally concatenated. Octogen discarded it and tried another URL source. |
| `canonical_cross_origin` | The canonical URL's hostname is neither the submitted hostname nor its parent or subdomain. This may indicate cross-site or incorrect product metadata. |
| `canonical_listing_page` | The canonical URL looks like a parent listing or category page. |
| `price_currency_missing` | A price was extracted without a currency. |
| `product_fields_clamped` | One or more extracted fields were adjusted to fit API limits—for example, long text was truncated, extra or invalid image URLs were removed, or a negative price was omitted. |

For shallow and client-HTML resolution, a missing canonical URL produces
`404 product_not_found`, not a warning in a successful response. Catalog
extraction can succeed with a null canonicalUrl. See the integration guide for selection rules, edge cases,
and recommended handling.
warnings.title: Warnings

ProgrammaticProductLookupRequest.description:
Programmatic product lookup request.

V1 supports URL lookup only. Keep the request body object-shaped so future
identifiers such as UUID can be added without overloading product search.

format.description: Response representation. json (default) returns the structured MerchantProductUrlLookupResponse envelope. md and markdown are equivalent aliases that return the product as LLM-ready Markdown using the same Python renderer as Cosimo.
format.title: Format

matchMode.description: Index match strictness. strict matches only exact/canonical URLs. loose (default) adds a lowest-priority fallback that ignores path case and query params, so a URL differing from an indexed product only by case (e.g. /Women/ vs /women/) or a non-indexed query param (e.g. Zara's ?v1=) still resolves. It also recognizes structural aliases: Shopify collection-scoped URLs (/collections/<x>/products/<handle>) resolve to the canonical /products/<handle> product. A strict/canonical hit always wins over a loose or alias one.
matchMode.title: Matchmode

onDemandCachePolicy.description: Cache behavior when the request enters the on-demand path.

resolutionMode.description: Source selection policy. auto checks the index before resolving on demand; index_only never performs outbound work; on_demand_only skips the index.

url.description: Product URL to look up in the organization's granted catalogs and, when enabled and requested, resolve on demand.

For follow-up lookups use normalizedUrl (indexed, catalog_extractor, and client_html results) or resolvedUrl (shallow on-demand results), not this field.

ProgrammaticProductSearchRequest.description:
Search indexed products by free text, filters, or both.

Each field controls one thing. ``q`` says what to find; ``facets``,
``exclude_facets`` and the bounds say what to keep; ``catalogs`` says
where to look; ``limit`` and ``cursor`` page. Combinations that would
contradict each other are rejected with 422 rather than resolved silently.

brand_quality_max.description: Inclusive maximum brand quality score, 1 to 6. Combined with any understood bound by keeping the stricter one.
brand_quality_max.title: Brand Quality Max

brand_quality_min.description: Inclusive minimum brand quality score, 1 (very poor) to 6 (exceptional). Combined with any understood bound by keeping the stricter one.
brand_quality_min.title: Brand Quality Min

catalogs.description: Catalog keys to search. Omit to search every catalog your key can access. Keys your key cannot access match nothing.
catalogs.title: Catalogs

cursor.description: `nextCursor` from the previous page, passed back verbatim with the same request body.
cursor.title: Cursor

debug.description: Include `effectiveQuery`: the text, filters and bounds that actually ran, with each facet's origin. It is a report, not a request fragment: understood facets of one name can AND together, which a request cannot express.
debug.title: Debug

exclude_facets.description: Filters a product must not match: products with any listed value of any listed facet are removed. Each name at most once.
exclude_facets.title: Exclude Facets

facets.description: Filters a product must match: every facet, and any value within a facet. A facet you send replaces any understood facet of the same name (a colour facet replaces both understood colour facets) and is never relaxed. Each name at most once.
facets.title: Facets

omit_generated_facets.description: Names of understood facets to drop before searching, for a derived filter that is wrong and that you have no value of your own for. To replace a derived filter instead, send a facet of that name. Use the names shown in `effectiveQuery`; colour is omitted per axis (`color` or `color_family`). Requires understood `q`; a name may not also appear in `facets`.
omit_generated_facets.title: Omit Generated Facets

price_max.description: Inclusive maximum price. Combined with any understood maximum by keeping the lower one.
price_max.title: Price Max

price_min.description: Inclusive minimum price. Combined with any understood minimum by keeping the higher one.
price_min.title: Price Min

q.description: Free-text query. Omit to browse by filters alone. By default it is understood: rewritten for retrieval, with category, gender, colour, brand, price and attribute filters derived from it. Blank is the same as omitted.
q.title: Q

relax.description: When an understood `q` returns nothing, retry with understood filters dropped in stages (inferred brand attributes, then attributes, then colour and deep categories) and return the first stage with results. Facets you send are never dropped. Requires understood `q`. A relaxed page's cursor continues the same relaxed results.
relax.title: Relax

similar_to_brands.description: Brand names whose style to favour. Ranks products by similarity to these brands' aesthetic; it does not filter. Replaces any brands understood from `q`.
similar_to_brands.title: Similar To Brands

understand.description: Run query understanding on `q`. Set false to match `q` as written and filter only by the facets and bounds you send. Requires `q`.
understand.title: Understand

ProgrammaticResolveFromHtmlRequest.description:
Resolve a product from caller-supplied HTML.

Stateless by contract: no index read, no outbound fetch, no caching — the
response is derived entirely from the submitted document.

html.description: Product page HTML to resolve. Capped at 5 MiB — the same bound the live on-demand fetch path enforces, so any page that path could retrieve is submittable here.
html.title: Html

url.description: Optional, but strongly recommended: the page's source URL, ideally location.href read at the same instant the DOM was serialized. It anchors relative image URLs and JSON-LD candidate selection exactly like the live path's final fetched URL, and it is echoed back as requestedUrl — on storefronts that record an in-page variant selection only in the URL's query parameters, this is the only variant-qualified identity the response retains. When absent the page itself must declare its canonical URL (JSON-LD Product/variant url, link rel=canonical, selected Offer.url, or og:url) or resolution fails with product_not_found.
url.title: Url

post.description:
Create a URL list.

Returns `201` with the list in `provisioning`: the list exists
synchronously — a stable `urlListId` you can immediately `GET` and add
URLs to — while its BigQuery resources are provisioned asynchronously
(`status` flips to `active` when they exist).

delete.description:
Delete a URL list.

Returns `202` with the list in `delete_pending`: access revocation and
resource teardown are asynchronous. There is no grace window and no
restore — the name is released immediately. Idempotent.

post.description:
Add URLs to the list — an idempotent set-add.

Each URL is normalized server-side; the normalized form is the
membership key. Invalid URLs come back per-URL in `rejected[]` on a
`200`. Adding a URL already present is an accepted no-op, so blind
re-syncs are safe. Capacity is batch-atomic: a batch that would cross
the 100,000-URL cap fails whole with `409`.

409.description: The list is being deleted, awaits the normalization-ruleset sweep (retryable within minutes), or — on add — the batch would cross the per-list URL cap (batch-atomic).

413.description: Request body over the byte-level size cap.

post.description:

Each input is normalized server-side before checking. A miss is

get.description:
List every host covered by an active crawled catalog.

A client caches this set (revalidating with ``If-None-Match``) and only
sends a URL to ``/products/lookup`` when its host is present, so
client-side coverage matching never disagrees with the server's own
coverage classification. Read-only and full-corpus, like search/lookup.

200.description: The covered-domain set (also returns the strong `ETag`).

304.description: The client's `If-None-Match` matches the current list; body is empty. Reuse the cached response.

503.description: Catalog registry unavailable (fail closed, safe to retry).

get.description:
Return the caller's own organization, key, quotas, and rate limit.

Read-only and side-effect free: safe to call on startup, in CI, and in a
health loop (subject to the ``/v1`` rate limit it reports). Never includes
key material — only the key id and its non-secret display prefix.

post.description: Resolve a product by URL: index first, then configured-catalog JIT or shallow resolution. One 45-second deadline bounds all tiers; no background indexing is dispatched. `POST /products/parse` is an exact alias. The response defaults to the structured JSON envelope; set `format` to `md` or `markdown` for the Python-rendered Markdown representation used by Cosimo.

200.description: The structured lookup envelope by default, or the product rendered as Markdown when format is md or markdown.

post.description:
Find products similar to a source product with a Catalog partner API key.

Full corpus by default: a ``catalogs`` allowlist in the request restricts
the RETRIEVAL to those catalogs, while source resolution always spans
every catalog the caller's resolved scope permits (the source may live
outside the allowlist). Every branch carries the scope, so a
``catalog_partner`` caller stays bounded to ``catalog_type = 'CRAWLED'``.

post.description:
Resolve a product from caller-supplied page HTML — no index or fetch.

Same shallow deterministic extraction as lookup's on-demand path
(JSON-LD → Open Graph → HTML meta), run over the submitted document
instead of a fetched one. Nothing is written to the product index or
resolver cache. A uniformly sampled subset of authenticated submissions,
including the supplied HTML and URL, may be retained for bounded internal
analysis.

404.description: The submitted HTML contains no credible product metadata, or no canonical product URL could be established (page declares none and no url was supplied).

429.description: Product resolution service-wide rate limit exceeded.

post.description:
Search indexed products by free text, filters, or both.

Results span every catalog your key can access unless `catalogs` narrows
them. Page 1 is ranked by relevance; later pages continue in quality-score
order from page 1's last result, so a product can repeat across pages —
de-duplicate by `uuid`.
